title: MRO Names
statement: Implement `solve()`. Build a diamond: D(B, C), B(A), C(A), A(object). Return the MRO class names of D, excluding `object`. Use the real C3 order Python computes. Do not hardcode a guess you did not check. You may call the classes.
constraints: Include D, B, C, and A
hints: Define the classes, then read D.__mro__.
Return the __name__ of each remaining class.

approaches.name: Direct
approaches.explanation: C3 linearization of this diamond visits D, then B, then C, then A.

editorial: C3 linearization of this diamond visits D, then B, then C, then A. B comes before C because D lists B first, and C is not a subclass of B so it is not skipped. Reading __mro__ is the check. Writing the list from memory and getting C before B is the usual miss.
